statement: Mixed step at negative states fails without the one-NOT hypothesis: on general_count_below_base_min (4 NOT gates, n=7) with OR-only F2 mixed slack, 146 of 248 negative states have no non-increasing paying step, and 0 of 281 nonnegative states fail; so any proof must use AtMostOneNot. Obstacle: minimality gives gates' >= base' at restrictions, the step needs |F2'| >= base'.

F2-transfer |F2'| >= base' holds at all 1,353,627 restrictions with base'>0 of 3,263 one-NOT circuits (n 4..10), 0 failures, NOT alive and killed both tight; the 4-NOT control reproduces A1's 248 negative states

F2 count at every mixed state with no DD set (one NOT gate, no minimality): |F2Mix(Q,D)| >= baseDQ; so base'-|F2'| <= sum over DD sets of (|S_w - D|-1). F2-transfer at (empty,empty) is no_minCE itself and a MinCE always has a DD set at the root; the open obstacle is DD-absorption (F2 gates outside non-DD unit merges pay for the DD sets), which holds at all 60,317 DD states of 98 stored one-NOT circuits (8,942 tight)
SAT: no circuit with at most 3 NOT gates and fewer than base gates on any of 224 OR-systems (n=4 all m; n=5 m=2..7 all, m=8 6 of 7; n=6 m=2,3); 448 UNSAT answers, no counterexample
MixedStep: no counterexample on 48 more irreducible read-NOT (no-rewire) circuits, n 7 to 9, 831,060 mixed states; no state of negative slack reached (least slack 0)

S3(b) Hall form holds for every circuit (any size, any number of NOT gates) on every system of at most two sets of size <= 3: outputs are private (dset_orS_le) and a triple's sole partner class is constant on its zero face (const_on_face), so it cannot also be a sole partner of a second triple (no_sole_partner). Lean core checked; the circuit-to-(first wire = A op B, B thin) step is paper.

S3(b) Hall form, exact SAT on functions (thin-basis relaxation: a Hall violation on W gives base(W)-1 AND/OR lines over W-thin functions computing every OR(S_w)): UNSAT on every subfamily of two3, dis3, two43, dis43, dis44, star44 (the t=4 C4w system), tri3, star3, tri4, q4, Pasch, so on these systems EVERY circuit, any size and any number of NOT gates, has >= base flip classes; controls with base(W) lines SAT. Stored circuits incl. t4/t5/t6: Hall holds on every subfamily, t4..t6 tight with 0 shared classes. Open: the thin-basis lemma in general (first unsettled: Fano, two 5-sets).

Thin-basis lemma via its single-point relaxation (the point lemma: sens at the all-zero point turns each line into a union/intersection/difference of partial transversals): exact SAT UNSAT at base-1 lines for two 5-sets sharing a point (26.9 s) and two disjoint 5-sets (16.4 s), Pasch (2.2 s); controls at base lines SAT (pasch, fano, two5, grid3). So S3(b) Hall form holds for every circuit, any number of NOT gates, on two 5-sets. Fano not finished in 300 s. B4's partition bound does not settle the acyclic thin-basis case (thin functions may depend on all inputs).

DD-absorption reduces to light absorption (one NOT gate, any mixed state): heavy atoms (h(1_Q+e_u)=1) of a DD set give |U_w|-1 OR merges in F2Mix at Zof(S_w u D), disjoint from every other top-zero-point unit merge set; so only the light atoms of DD sets are unpaid. No counterexample to DD-absorption or light absorption: 0 failures at 149,861 sampled DD states of 2,393 stored circuits n<=16 (up to 19 DD sets) and at all 1,147,168 DD states for n<=11. Obstacle: light unit merges at 1_Q overlap between DD sets.

Density form of |F2|, base, slack: base = sum_k (k-1) N_k exactly; F2 = #{OR gates with a witness context Z in D_g} exactly (F2(Q)=sum_g 1[Q in a down-set D_g], verified all Q n<=9, Phi at p=1/3 exact); witness tuple contains a cube point Z so it is not a bounded-size pattern; Z=0 relational form is only a lower bound (misses 7/12 on c4mono, 21/30 on pasch_mono, 6/21 on twin trees); Bonferroni P1-P2 <= F2 <= P1 holds exactly on 17/17 circuits; slack>=0 iff sum_{j>=1} d_j >= sum_k (k-1) a_k (exact, no o(n) loss).

Point lemma for two sets S, T (|S∩T|<=1): every program of union/intersection/difference lines over partial transversals with S and T among its lines has >= |S|+|T|-2 lines when min(|S|,|T|) <= 2 (tight-tree lemma); exact SAT UNSAT at |S|+|T|-3 lines for all size pairs with |S|+|T| <= 10 (new (4,6), (3,7)). General case open: the bound fails with XOR as an op (any proof must use monotonicity); one-point gate elimination (rule R) is false; open step is rule R2 (point or S/T pair removal).

A10: light absorption reduced (paper) to BOTTOM PAY: unit runs of DD sets at the bottom 1_Q (heavy atoms pre-joined) give |T_w|-[U_w empty] OR merges, each F2 with witness 1_Q (pays the bridge); light absorption follows from disjoint such payments outside the top family. BOTTOM PAY (forest/matroid-union form) holds with 0 failures at 136,843 (n<=9 all states) + 119,467 (n<=16 sampled) + 1,010,325 (switch circuits) DD states. Obstacle: bottom runs of two DD sets overlap (2,775 states n<=9) and no one-zero-point-per-set choice in {h=0} avoids it (242 states); payment needs a matching-style re-choice. No proof.

PHC@0 (payment Hall condition at the common point 0: the lines of a point program split into disjoint spanning forests, one per set) implies the point lemma and contains BottomPay as the instance at 1_Q; 0 failures, exhaustive over line values at base lines for two sets of sizes (2,3),(3,3),(3,4),(4,4),(3,5) shared and disjoint and tri3, star3; 0 failures on 21 stored circuits (0-6 NOT gates). The OR-only form (as in BottomPay) is refuted for free difference: 5-line program for |S|=2,|T|=4 disjoint; it held on all sampled monotone programs.

Rule R2 of B9 s3.2 (in every program with S, T among its lines, one private point deletes >= 1 line after cleanup or one private pair a in S, e in T deletes >= 2) is false: exact SAT witnesses with no redundant or dead line at (3,5) disjoint and shared with 8 lines and (4,4) disjoint with 9 lines, each re-checked by two independent cleanup counts; R2 holds (UNSAT) at every run with K <= base + 1. The point lemma is not affected (it needs R2 only below base). PHC@0 holds on the three smallest counterexamples.
